question: What claim about the authority by which the yoginī named Icchā extends to the end of Māyā is entailed by attributing it to the siddhas and to supreme will?
premises: The yoginī named Icchā is referenced.
She extends to the end of Māyā.
This is by the siddhas and by supreme will.
inference: The yoginī Icchā extends to the end of Māyā by the agency of the siddhas and by supreme will.
uncertainties: The precise relation between the siddhas and supreme will is not specified here.
plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by the siddhas and by supreme will, extends to the end of Māyā.
